SAP Activate methodology phases.snippet:
**SAP Activate Methodology phases**: D-P-E-R-D-R
Discover ------> Prepare ------> Explore ------> Realize ------> Deploy ------> Run
1. In the **Discovery** phase, customers become familiar with the benefits of the solution.
Preliminary project assessment of the solution options is performed and, once the customer understands the solution, they begin the trial of the solution.
2. In the **Prepare** phase, we define project governance, start the project, define/identify the resources, define the roles and responsibilities for the project team, and detail the management plans for running the project.
3. In the **Explore** phase, we run the fit-to-standard analysis on the working system with the best practices content up and running.
The objective of the Explore phase is to identify the fit of the best practices-based solution, capture delta configuration requirements, identify gaps, and configuration values.
All these are captured by the project team in the backlog and later, in Realize phase, the backlog items are implemented in the system.
The best practices content is used as a jump-start for the project.
4.
During the **Realize** phase, the project team will use agile approach to iteratively and incrementally build the functionality from the backlog.
This build follows the prioritization given by the product owner (for example, the business users) that continue to be involved with the project team during the sprints.
During the build the team completes the remaining configuration and development on top of the best practices content.
Additionally, the team performs the unit and string testing during the sprints.
In the Realize phase, the team also works on the integration of the overall solution to meet customer needs.
The Realize phase covers all the build and test activities required to prepare a release of functionality into production.
This includes a full Integration test and user acceptance test before the team can continue into the Deploy phase.
5. The objective of the **Deploy** phase is to launch the production environment and confirm readiness to switch into business operations with the new solution.
The team also performs sustainment and hyper-care activities in the Deploy phase once the system goes live.
Once the customer has switched over into the new environment, the project team supports the customer IT and business.
The team stay on-site for a pre-determined period of time, which is usually defined in the contract or agreed as part of the plan to transition to operations.
6. The **Run** phase then represents key steps in running and improving the operations of the environment.
This includes end user support, system monitoring and other activities including continuous improvements to the solution.

L'exécution correspond efficacement au support ou à la gestion de la solution de production après la mise en production.
SAP dispose de plusieurs normes pour l'exécution optimale d'une solution, qui vont de la gestion des incidents et des modifications, la surveillance des systèmes et des applications à la gestion des montées de version.
Il y a 16 normes au total.

SAP Cloud ALM AI features 2025.title: AI in SAP Cloud ALM Takes Monitoring to Another Level
SAP Cloud ALM AI features 2025.snippet:
SAP Cloud ALM Synthetic User Monitoring is a 24/7 monitoring solution that enables customers to detect performance and availability issues of Web Applications from a client-side perspective.
...
So how did the engineers use AI to improve Synthetic User Monitoring exactly?
Well this is where **dynamic threshold setting** comes into the picture.
Instead of having to configure fixed thresholds for monitoring and alerting critical performance situations, AI can now be used to automatically compute and predict dynamic thresholds for the upcoming periods based on historical execution durations, all the while taking data seasonality into account.
As they gain insights and experience, users can then adjust the sensitivity of the thresholds to **optimize the process even further**, saving a lot of time and many headaches in the process.
...
So that’s one type of user monitoring already benefitting from AI infused technology, but what about Real User Monitoring?
For any readers unfamiliar with this tool, SAP Cloud ALM Real User Monitoring provides IT and business analysts with **transparency** regarding the performance that is experienced by **actual end users**, as well as information about the utilization of business functionality.
...
One challenge of using Real User Monitoring, however, is that sometimes the alerting can be *too* sensitive.
But by infusing AI into the process, a **latency** can be introduced so that alerts are no longer generated on the first data point.
Furthermore, thresholds can be fixed and **no longer need to be maintained manually**.
Instead, the distribution of data points is analyzed and compared against reference periods.
Only when an unexpected and notable situation continues for a certain period of time is it then considered as “critical” and worthy of generating an alert, leading to more accurate and valid alerting and less disruption for the users responsible.
...
As we look to the very near future, adding further AI solutions for **content generation**, reducing **configuration efforts**, enabling **automatic data analysis**, and facilitating **proactive actions ** to SAP Cloud ALM will break new ground in helping to boost user productivity, accelerate alert resolution, and simplify project delivery and execution – by generating crucial project artifacts like documents or requirements, to name just one example.
